attempted_claim: Let M be a fixed finite-volume orientable two-cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold (in particular, a two-component hyperbolic link complement), with cusp shapes tau_1,tau_2 such that 1,tau_1,tau_2,tau_1 tau_2 are linearly independent over Q. For the hyperbolic simultaneous Dehn filling M_{p_1/q_1,p_2/q_2}, where each slope is represented by a coprime integer pair, does there exist a constant c_M>0 such that every sufficiently long filling satisfies [K(M_{p_1/q_1,p_2/q_2}):Q] >= (1/c_M) max{|p_1|,|q_1|,|p_2|,|q_2|}? Here K(·) is the ordinary trace field, and “sufficiently long” means that all four displayed absolute values tend to infinity in the usual hyperbolic Dehn-filling regime; no conditional hypothesis such as Lehmer’s conjecture is part of the question.
decisive_failure: The investigation establishes a documented negative result, not a theorem: it shows every available route to the unconditional linear trace-field bound is structurally blocked (missing global conjugate upper bound; Dobrowolski polylog gap computed to grow unboundedly; two-scale uniformity failing by fiber freedom; closest literature Lehmer-conditional), formalized by two executed scripts. It does not disprove the target claim, which remains open, and the conditional diagnostic does not substitute for a proof. No emergent claim is made.
